newsitem.title: USA: Kansas legislature wraps session, FY 1998 spending.
newsitem.headline: Kansas legislature wraps session, FY 1998 spending.

text.p: Kansas lawmakers have approved a $3.84 billion general fund budget and total spending of $7.99 billion for the fiscal year 1998 beginning on July 1, an assistant to the House Speaker said Tuesday.

The legislature completed its refinements of the budget early Tuesday, approving an omnibus spending package that also includes planning money for expanding two state prisons, John Potter said, an assistant to the House Speaker .
Legislators approved $677,000 for planning and authorized up to $6.8 million of bonds to expand the Hutchinson and Norton prisons by 200 beds each, Potter said.

Legislators had completed most of the budget by early April, but adjourned until late April when they could not resolve several conflicts, including the use of local option funding for school budgets and proposals to ban partial-birth abortion methods in the third trimester.
Legislators moved to extend the local option budget for school districts for the upcoming academic year if they already operate under a voter-approved option.

The plan approved by the legislature would call for the local option budget to be phased out over the next three years and require new voter approval for it to be initiated or continued in the future.
Proposals to ban partial-birth abortion failed when a conference committee could not resolve conflicts between the house and senate versions, Potter said.
The spending plan and the local option budget extension have been forwarded to Kansas Gov. Bill Graves, who proposed a $3.75 billion general fund budget in January.
Graves had sought funding for 500 new prison beds. He signed a $117 million property tax relief package and $36 million school funding increase in early April.
